memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early the next morning Joshua mustered his army, and he and the leaders of Israel marched before them to Ai. The entire force that was with him marched up and approached the city and arrived in front of it. They set up camp north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city. Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city. So the soldiers took up their positions — with the main camp to the north of the city and the ambush to the west of it. That night Joshua went into the valley. — Josh 8:10-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again we read that Joshua "got up early." This is a recurring detail in his life — he rises early to do the work of God. There is something to learn from this quiet habit. Joshua did not drag his feet or delay obedience. When there was God's work to be done, he was up and at it, ready and eager. Diligence and promptness marked his walk with God.

Notice too the careful positioning of the forces — the main camp to the north, the ambush to the west, everyone exactly where they needed to be. Everything was arranged with intention. And then, tellingly, "that night Joshua went into the valley." The leader did not hang back in safety; he placed himself among his people, in the thick of it, sharing their risk. That is the mark of a true shepherd-leader.

Behind all this careful positioning, though, we must remember the deeper truth. All the strategy in the world would accomplish nothing without God's promise that He would give the city into their hands. The planning was good and right, but it was God who would win the battle. Human preparation and divine power work together, but the power is always God's.

There is encouragement here for us. God honours diligence and careful obedience, yet He never asks us to carry the outcome ourselves. We take our positions faithfully, we do our part with intention, and we trust God for the victory. Like Joshua going down into the valley, our Saviour did not stay at a safe distance but entered fully into our struggle, even into the valley of death, for our sake (Heb 2:14-15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you prompt and diligent in the work God gives you, like Joshua rising early?
2. Do you lead or serve from a safe distance, or do you enter in alongside others?
3. How does it comfort you that Christ entered fully into our struggle, even the valley?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me prompt and diligent in Your work. Help me not to hang back in safety but to serve wholeheartedly, trusting You for the outcome. Amen.
